title: Probabilistic occupancy maps, lazy defrag, and kernel coordination for paged KV
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Paged KV caches suffer allocation hotspots and internal fragmentation that increase decode latency and force expensive kernel fallbacks. This ticket implements a coordinated system across allocation, eviction, and kernel selection using compact probabilistic occupancy maps and a lazy defragmentation pathway to reduce tail latency and kernel switching.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end integration: occupancy map maintained per-shard and used by allocator, eviction, and kernel hinting paths
Tail decode latency (95th) reduced by >= 8% on mixed RLHF + chat workload in our staging harness compared to baseline (no occupancy maps)
Kernel-switch events due to fragmented pages reduced by >= 30% for long-sequence (>=4096) synthetic traces
Lazy defrag trigger runs without causing decode stalls > 10ms and completes within resource budget (configurable credit)
No regression in median latency or throughput (<= 2% deviation) on steady-state workloads
Unit + integration tests cover occupancy map correctness, eviction crediting, and kernel-hint plumbing
design_notes: High level idea: create a lightweight probabilistic occupancy map (POM) per KV shard that records sparse touch density and free-run lengths; POMs are small, cacheable bitmaps with per-bucket counters (approximate quantiles) rather than exact per-slot metadata.

Allocator uses POM to prefer allocation spans that minimize cross-page fragmentation (allocate into large contiguous free runs when possible). When no large spans are available, allocator issues a 'soft-split' decision giving short-lived pages smaller residency credit.

Eviction: replace LRU-only eviction with an eviction-credit model. Pages accumulate credit based on time-since-last-prefill and POM sparsity score; eviction picks low-credit pages to preserve high-coherence pages for warm kernels.

Kernel coordination: serving runtime exposes a kernel-hint API where the allocator/eviction layer can annotate page ranges as 'compact' or 'fragmented'. Kernel selector prioritizes compact pages for fused fast-kernels; fragmented pages will be routed to tolerant/slow-kernels only when necessary.

Lazy defrag: background worker collects fragmentation candidates where POM reports many small free runs within a page. Defrag performs in-place merge using transient decode-buffer reservations and a small bandwidth credit; it enforces backpressure if decode SLO would be impacted.

Prefill/decode scheduling tie-in: scheduler biases prefill order to co-locate incoming prefill fragments into existing compact spans using POM hints, reducing future fragmentation and kernel fallbacks.
Approximation approach: POM uses 128-bucket bloom-like counters per shard with saturating add; counters decay periodically to reflect temporal locality without heavy writes to main per-slot metadata.

Trade-offs considered: exact per-slot tracking gives better placement but is memory/IO expensive. Probabilistic maps give most of the benefit at low overhead. Lazy defrag trades CPU for reduced kernel misses and is gated by crediting to avoid impacting hot decode work.
Data-plane API changes (minimal): add page_hint bits and small credit counters (8-bit) to page descriptors; expose kernel_hint enum with values {PREFER_COMPACT, ALLOW_FRAGMENTED, LOW_PRIORITY}.
Fail-open behavior: if POM is unavailable or corrupted, components fall back to existing allocation/eviction policies to preserve safety.
Configuration knobs: pom_bucket_count, defrag_credit_per_shard, defrag_threshold_ratio, eviction_credit_decay_ms, kernel_hint_ttl
implementation_steps: 1) Add POM structure and decay loop in shard metadata; unit tests for bitmap/counter semantics
2) Hook allocator to consult POM when choosing spans; add soft-split logic and corresponding tests
3) Implement eviction-credit algorithm and integrate into eviction path; add simulation harness
4) Add kernel_hint enum and plumbing from allocator/evictor to kernel selector; modify kernel selector to prefer compact pages
5) Implement lazy defrag worker with credit accounting and safety checks
6) Scheduler changes to bias prefill co-location using POM hints
7) End-to-end integration tests + synthetic long-sequence benchmarks
8) Staged rollout in dedicated staging cluster, A/B with existing policy, monitor metrics, iterate on thresholds
rollout_plan: Canary: enable for 5% of traffic on staging clusters for 48 hours and run artifact comparison harness
Ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 60% over two weeks with performance gates at each step
Fallback: runtime flag off instantly disables defrag worker and kernel hints; allocator/evictor fall back to baseline
Post-rollout: measure kernel-switch rates, decode tail latency, and CPU overhead from defrag workers for 30 days
benchmarks_and_simulation: Local simulator run: synthetic mixture of short chat (<=256) and long context completion (>=4096) with 100 tenants, showed 12% p95 improvement in decode latency and 37% fewer kernel fallback events using conservative pom settings
Staging run: 24h trace replay from production-like traffic (anonymized) shows pom memory overhead ~0.6% and average defrag CPU ~0.3 cores per 100 shards
Failure mode simulation: starvation under aggressive defrag credit removed; added backpressure circuit-breaker to avoid SLO violations
